name: Amazon
description: Targeted placement preparation for Amazon covering Amazon SDE Hiring patterns and enterprise technical standards.
common_roles: Java Developer, Python Developer, Data Analyst, Software Engineer
hiring_rounds: Online Assessment (2 Coding + Work Simulation) -> 3 Technical Rounds -> Bar Raiser Round
aptitude_pattern: Work Simulation Assessment + Complex Tradeoff Reasoning + AWS Throughput Math (75 mins)
coding_pattern: Medium/Hard Algorithmic Challenges (Trees, Graphs, Priority Queues, Dynamic Programming) - 70 mins
technical_focus: Low-Level Object Oriented Design (Parking Lot, Locker), SQS/SNS event decoupling, Lambda cold starts, blast radius reduction
hr_tips: Strictly format every answer using the STAR method mapped directly to Amazon 16 Leadership Principles
recommended_skills: Java, Python, AWS (DynamoDB, SQS, Lambda), Distributed Systems, System Design, DSA

questions.question: An AWS Lambda function processes requests with average execution time 180ms and memory allocation 512MB. If Amazon receives 2.5 million requests per hour, what is the total gigabyte-seconds (GB-s) consumed in that hour?
questions.explanation: Total execution time = 2,500,000 * 0.180s = 450,000 seconds. Memory in GB = 512 / 1024 = 0.5 GB. Total GB-s = 450,000 * 0.5 = 225,000 GB-s.

questions.question: An Amazon fulfillment center sorting conveyor runs at 3.2 meters/sec. Packages are spaced every 80 centimeters. If the scanner rejects 4% of packages due to barcode smudge, how many packages successfully pass through every 15 minutes?
questions.explanation: Packages per second = 3.2 m/s / 0.8 m = 4 pkgs/sec. In 15 minutes (900s): total = 900 * 4 = 3600 packages. Successful (96%) = 3600 * 0.96 = 3,456 packages.

questions.question: Amazon DynamoDB provisioned throughput is set to 800 WCU (Write Capacity Units). Standard writes (< 1KB) consume 1 WCU, while transactional writes consume 2 WCU. If 60% of writes are standard and 40% are transactional, what is the maximum total write requests per second achievable?
questions.explanation: Average WCU per write = 0.60 * 1 + 0.40 * 2 = 1.4 WCU. Maximum writes/sec = 800 / 1.4 = 571.4 writes/sec.

questions.question: In Amazon S3, standard storage availability SLA is 99.99% per month. In a 30-day month (43,200 minutes), what is the maximum permissible total downtime before an SLA credit is triggered?
questions.explanation: Downtime allowed = 43,200 minutes * (1 - 0.9999) = 43,200 * 0.0001 = 4.32 minutes per month.

questions.question: An Amazon seller increases product price by 25% for holiday surge, then offers a 20% discount coupon. Compared to the original baseline price, what is the net price percentage change?
questions.explanation: Let price = 100. Increased = 125. Discount = 20% of 125 = 25. Final price = 100. Net change = 0%.

questions.question: An Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group has a scale-out policy triggered when average CPU > 75%. Currently 4 instances run at [80%, 70%, 90%, 60%] CPU. What must the 5th instance's CPU be to bring the cluster average down to exactly 65%?
questions.explanation: Current total CPU = 80 + 70 + 90 + 60 = 300%. For 5 instances with average 65%: total needed = 5 * 65 = 325%. 5th instance = 325 - 300 = 25%.

questions.question: A retail warehouse worker can pack 18 small parcels/hr or 12 large parcels/hr. In an 8-hour shift, if the worker packs twice as many small parcels as large parcels, how many total parcels were packed?
questions.explanation: Let x be number of large parcels, 2x small parcels. Time for large = x / 12, time for small = 2x / 18 = x / 9. Total time: x/12 + x/9 = 7x/36 = 8 hours => x ≈ 41 large, 82 small = approx 120-123 parcels.

questions.question: An AWS Kinesis Data Stream has 4 shards. Each shard supports up to 1 MB/s write and 2 MB/s read. If 2 consumer applications independently read the stream in real-time, what is the maximum aggregated write capacity before sharding is required?
questions.explanation: Write capacity is strictly 1 MB/s per shard regardless of consumer count. With 4 shards: 4 * 1 MB/s = 4 MB/s.

questions.question: Amazon SQS standard queue delivers messages at least once. If duplicate probability is 2% per message, what is the probability that in a batch of 10 messages, at least one message is delivered duplicate?
An Amazon Prime delivery route has 6 stops. If Stop A must always be visited strictly before Stop B, in how many different valid orderings can the driver complete the route?
questions.explanation: Total unconstrained permutations = 6! = 720. In exactly half of these permutations, A appears before B by symmetry. 720 / 2 = 360 valid orderings.

questions.question: An e-commerce flash sale server experiences traffic scaling according to T(t) = 500 + 40t - 2t^2 requests/sec. At what time t (in seconds) does peak request throughput occur?
questions.explanation: Derivative T'(t) = 40 - 4t. Setting to 0: 4t = 40 => t = 10 seconds. Peak throughput is T(10) = 500 + 400 - 200 = 700 req/s.

questions.question: Amazon Aurora database replication clones data across 3 Availability Zones with 6 copies. For a write to succeed, a quorum of 4 out of 6 nodes must acknowledge. If each node has a 98% write success rate, what is the probability that write quorum is achieved?
questions.explanation: Binomial distribution for n=6, p=0.98, k>=4. The likelihood of having 3 or more failures is negligible: C(6,3)*0.02^3 ≈ 0.00016. Success probability is 99.98%.

questions.question: A product recommendation engine computes cosine similarity between user vector U=[3, 4] and product vector V=[4, 3]. What is the exact cosine similarity?
questions.explanation: Dot product = 3*4 + 4*3 = 12 + 12 = 24. Magnitude U = sqrt(9+16)=5. Magnitude V = sqrt(16+9)=5. Cosine similarity = 24 / (5 * 5) = 24 / 25 = 0.96.

questions.question: A team of 6 engineers must be divided into a 2-pizza team of at least 3 but at most 5 engineers. How many different valid sub-teams can be selected?
questions.explanation: Valid team sizes are 3, 4, 5. C(6, 3) = 20, C(6, 4) = 15, C(6, 5) = 6. Total ways = 20 + 15 + 6 = 41 ways.

questions.question: An AWS CloudFront edge location has an 85% cache hit ratio. Cached responses take 15ms while cache misses fetch from origin taking 120ms. What is the average latency experienced by end users?

questions.explanation: Amazon warehouse priority queue: Count character frequencies, use a Max-Heap to alternate placing the most frequent characters.

questions.question: Given an m x n 2D binary grid representing a map of '1's (land/storage bins) and '0's (water/aisles), return the number of connected islands.
questions.explanation: Standard Amazon BFS/DFS: Traverse grid, sink visited land cells to '0', count connected components.

extra.title: Number of Islands (Fulfillment Center Grid)

questions.question: There are n servers numbered from 0 to n - 1 and a list of connections. A critical connection is a connection that, if removed, will make some server unable to reach some other server. Find all critical connections (Tarjan's algorithm).
questions.explanation: Tarjan's Bridge-Finding algorithm using discovery times and low-link values in a single DFS pass.

extra.title: Critical Connections in an AWS Network

questions.question: Given an array of meeting time intervals consisting of start and end times [[s1,e1],[s2,e2],...], find the minimum number of conference rooms required.
questions.explanation: Sort intervals by start time and maintain a Min-Heap of end times, or separate and sort start/end arrays.

extra.title: Meeting Rooms II (Conference Scheduling)

questions.question: Given an array of points where points[i] = [xi, yi] represents a delivery destination on the X-Y plane and an integer k, return the k closest points to the origin (0, 0).
questions.explanation: Maintain a Max-Heap of size K storing Euclidean distances, or use QuickSelect for O(N) average time.

extra.title: K Closest Points to Amazon Fulfillment Center

questions.question: Given the roots of two binary trees root and subRoot, return true if there is a subtree of root with the same structure and node values of subRoot.
questions.explanation: Recursive tree traversal with isSameTree helper check, or serialize trees using Merkle hashing.

extra.title: Subtree of Another Tree

questions.question: You are given a string s. We want to partition the string into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part. Return a list of integers representing the size of these parts.
questions.explanation: Record last occurrence index of each character, then greedy scan expanding current partition boundary.

extra.title: Partition Labels (Amazon Order Batching)

questions.question: You are given an m x n grid containing values 0 (empty), 1 (fresh), or 2 (rotten). Every minute, any fresh orange that is 4-directionally adjacent to a rotten orange becomes rotten. Return the minimum number of minutes until no fresh orange remains.
questions.explanation: Multi-source BFS starting with all initially rotten oranges in queue, tracking elapsed minutes layer by layer.

extra.title: Rotten Oranges (Inventory Spoilage)

questions.question: Explain the principles of DynamoDB Single-Table Design. How do Partition Keys (PK) and Sort Keys (SK) enable multiple 1-to-N entity relationships in a single table?
questions.explanation: Single-Table design models all application entities into one table using overloaded generic PK and SK (e.g. USER#101, ORDER#502). Global Secondary Indexes (GSIs) provide alternate access patterns, avoiding distributed joins.

questions.question: How does Amazon handle decoupling between microservices using AWS SQS (Simple Queue Service) and SNS (Simple Notification Service) in the Fan-Out pattern?
questions.explanation: SNS acts as pub/sub topic; multiple SQS queues subscribe to it. Each downstream service processes messages asynchronously at its own pace without coupling publisher to subscriber availability.

questions.question: In AWS Lambda serverless applications, what factors cause cold starts, and what architectural strategies (Provisioned Concurrency, SnapStart) mitigate them?
questions.explanation: Cold start occurs when AWS initializes a new microVM execution environment, downloads package, and starts language runtime (JVM/Node). SnapStart snapshots initialized memory to fire up execution in sub-100ms.

questions.explanation: Use decentralized optimistic locking, in-memory distributed Redis caches with Lua atomic scripts for inventory reservation, and asynchronous message queues to persist confirmed orders to DynamoDB.

questions.question: Explain Low-Level Object Oriented Design for an Amazon Locker delivery system. What classes, interfaces, and design patterns (State, Strategy) would you implement?
questions.explanation: Classes: LockerHub, LockerBox (size: S/M/L, state: Available/Occupied), Package, PinCodeToken. Strategy pattern for optimal locker assignment; State pattern for locker lifecycle management.

questions.question: What is 'Blast Radius Reduction' in Amazon AWS microservices architecture, and how do Cell-Based Architectures limit customer impact during catastrophic failures?
questions.explanation: Cell-based architecture partitions users into self-contained independent failure domains ('cells'). If an outage hits Cell 4, only 5% of users are affected while the remaining 95% continue functioning without degradation.

questions.question: Compare Amazon Aurora's distributed storage architecture with traditional MySQL on EBS volumes. How does Aurora achieve 5x write throughput?
questions.explanation: Aurora separates compute from storage. Compute nodes write only Redo Log records to a 6-way replicated storage fleet across 3 AZs. Storage nodes apply logs asynchronously in background, eliminating double-write buffers.

extra.company_focus: 16 Leadership Principles, AWS cloud architecture, DynamoDB single-table design, high-throughput microservices, customer obsession

questions.question: How do you guarantee idempotency in Amazon API payment and order submission endpoints when client network timeouts cause duplicate retries?
questions.explanation: Clients generate unique Idempotency Keys (UUIDv4) passed in HTTP headers. The API Gateway/backend checks DynamoDB with conditional write before processing; duplicate requests return the cached original response.

extra.company_focus: 16 Leadership Principles, AWS cloud architecture, DynamoDB single-table design, high-throughput microservices, customer obsession

questions.question: Explain Eventual Consistency vs Strong Consistency in Amazon S3 and DynamoDB. What tradeoffs exist in terms of latency, cost, and availability?
questions.explanation: Strong consistency guarantees reading the latest write at the cost of higher latency and 2x read capacity units (in DynamoDB). Eventual consistency reads immediately from any replica, which may briefly return stale data.

extra.company_focus: 16 Leadership Principles, AWS cloud architecture, DynamoDB single-table design, high-throughput microservices, customer obsession

questions.question: Describe the internal mechanics of Amazon SQS Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) and Redrive Policies for poison pill message handling in distributed pipelines.
questions.explanation: Messages exceeding maxReceiveCount without being successfully acknowledged and deleted are automatically routed to a DLQ. This unblocks the queue from crashing consumers and permits debugging or reprocessing.

extra.company_focus: 16 Leadership Principles, AWS cloud architecture, DynamoDB single-table design, high-throughput microservices, customer obsession

questions.question: How does Amazon API Gateway implement Token Bucket rate limiting, and how do you protect internal services from sudden DDoS or thundering herd spikes?
questions.explanation: Token Bucket algorithm maintains a bucket of size B filled with r tokens per second. Requests deduct 1 token. When bucket is empty, requests return 429 Too Many Requests, shielding backends from saturation.

extra.company_focus: 16 Leadership Principles, AWS cloud architecture, DynamoDB single-table design, high-throughput microservices, customer obsession

questions.question: In Java Spring Boot services deployed on AWS ECS Fargate, how do you tune HikariCP database connection pooling to prevent RDS connection exhaustion?
questions.explanation: Formula: Pool Size = (Core_Count * 2) + Effective_Spindle_Count. In containerized microservices with multiple tasks, max pool size per container must be capped so sum of tasks <= RDS max_connections.

questions.question: How does AWS Secrets Manager handle automatic database credential rotation without service downtime or broken application connections?
questions.explanation: A Lambda function creates a secondary DB user, tests connectivity, updates Secrets Manager, swaps credentials in client connection pool gracefully, and deprecates the old user in rotation cycle.

extra.company_focus: 16 Leadership Principles, AWS cloud architecture, DynamoDB single-table design, high-throughput microservices, customer obsession

questions.question: Explain the difference between AWS ECS (Elastic Container Service) and EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service). In what enterprise scenarios would you choose ECS over EKS?
questions.explanation: ECS is AWS-native with simpler configuration and deep AWS IAM/VPC integration. EKS provides full Kubernetes compatibility for hybrid multi-cloud portability and extensive open-source CNCF ecosystem tools.

questions.question: How do you implement Distributed Tracing across 15 microservices in Amazon AWS using AWS X-Ray and OpenTelemetry?
questions.explanation: Propagate 'X-Amzn-Trace-Id' HTTP headers across service boundaries. Instrument HTTP clients, database drivers, and messaging queues with OpenTelemetry SDK to assemble comprehensive request traces.

extra.company_focus: 16 Leadership Principles, AWS cloud architecture, DynamoDB single-table design, high-throughput microservices, customer obsession

questions.question: How would you integrate Amazon Bedrock foundation models into an e-commerce catalog search service with Claude 3 and Titan Embeddings to implement conversational shopping?
questions.explanation: Explain: 1) Vector search in OpenSearch Service, 2) Multi-turn conversation state in DynamoDB, 3) Prompt engineering for product recommendation guardrails, 4) Real-time pricing lookup with Bedrock Tools.

questions.question: How do you utilize Amazon Q Developer / CodeWhisperer to improve team velocity while preventing copyright or security vulnerability contamination in proprietary codebases?
questions.explanation: Discuss: Enabling Reference Tracker to detect matching public code, configuring automated security scans for OWASP vulnerabilities, and auditing AI-generated pull requests before merge.

questions.question: Describe how you design cost-effective generative AI inference workloads on AWS using AWS Inferentia2 and Trainium chips compared to standard Nvidia GPUs.
questions.explanation: Detail: Neuron SDK compilation, FP8 and BF16 quantization, latency benchmarking, and Auto Scaling based on real-time token generation throughput.

questions.question: How do you implement Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock to automatically redact sensitive PII (credit cards, phone numbers) and prevent competitive product mentions?
questions.explanation: Detail: Setting up Bedrock Guardrail filters with contextual grounding checks, denied topics, word filters, and sensitive information redaction masks.

questions.question: Explain how you build an automated customer review sentiment extraction and aspect-based summarization pipeline using Amazon Comprehend and SageMaker.
questions.explanation: Architecture: Review stream pushed to Kinesis, processed by Comprehend for targeted sentiment and entity extraction, aggregated into Amazon Timestream for dashboard analytics.

questions.question: How do you evaluate model drift and data distribution shifts in an Amazon retail demand forecasting model deployed on Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor?
questions.explanation: Discuss: Baseline statistical constraints generated from training data, monitoring S3 endpoint traffic captures, and alerting when Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance exceeds threshold.

questions.question: How would you implement a high-scale Vector Database solution on AWS using Amazon OpenSearch Serverless for 50 million product vectors?
questions.explanation: Detail: HNSW and IVF indexing algorithms, sharding strategy, memory provisioning, cold/warm storage tiers, and hybrid vector + BM25 keyword search.

questions.question: Describe the architecture of an agentic workflow on Amazon Bedrock Agents that autonomously coordinates delivery rescheduling with logistics APIs.
questions.explanation: Structure: OpenAPI schema definition, Lambda action groups, conversational memory, reasoning prompt templates, and human escalation handoff rules.

questions.question: How do you enforce multi-tenant isolation and strict data governance when hosting LLM-based microservices for enterprise AWS B2B clients?
questions.explanation: Explain: Tenant-specific encryption keys with AWS KMS, IAM session policies, partitioned vector namespaces, and zero cross-tenant prompt leakage.

questions.question: How do you use Amazon SageMaker Clarify to detect algorithmic bias and feature importance in automated credit or seller approval algorithms?
questions.explanation: Discuss: Disparate impact metrics, counterfactual fairness analysis, SHAP (Shapley Additive exPlanations) values, and regulatory compliance reporting.

questions.question: Amazon's core Leadership Principle is 'Customer Obsession'. Can you describe a project where you prioritized long-term customer experience over an easy engineering shortcut?
questions.explanation: Use STAR: Detail customer pain point, quantify positive customer outcome, and explain how you advocated for the customer despite engineering pressure.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you demonstrated 'Ownership' by stepping up to resolve an issue that was clearly outside your designated responsibilities or team charter.
questions.explanation: Demonstrate: 'Leaders are owners. They never say that's not my job.' Show proactive resolution of an orphaned problem with measurable organizational benefit.

questions.question: Describe an instance where you demonstrated 'Bias for Action' by making a critical architectural or product decision with incomplete information.
questions.explanation: Highlight: Calculated risk taking, two-way door decisions (reversible) vs one-way doors, gathering key signals quickly, and executing without analysis paralysis.

questions.question: Tell me about a situation where you had to 'Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit' with a senior colleague or manager regarding a technical approach.
questions.explanation: Explain: Professional respectful defense of your conviction backed by data, listening to counterarguments, and committing 100% once the decision was made.

extra.hr_dimension: Amazon LP: Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit

questions.question: How do you embody 'Invent and Simplify'? Describe a complex software process, deployment pipeline, or system that you radically streamlined.
questions.explanation: Focus on: Removing unnecessary dependencies, cutting latency or cloud costs, and simplifying architecture so other engineers can easily maintain it.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you missed an important milestone or deliverable. How did you 'Deliver Results' and rebuild stakeholder trust?
questions.explanation: Emphasize: Radical transparency, early communication of slippage, mitigating root causes, and executing an aggressive turnaround plan.

questions.question: Describe a time you demonstrated 'Frugality' by accomplishing a significant engineering milestone with limited compute resources, budget, or tools.
questions.explanation: Highlight: Resourcefulness, optimizing cloud spend, utilizing open-source tools effectively, and doing more with less.

questions.question: How do you 'Earn Trust' of team members and stakeholders when joining a new high-velocity engineering team with an established codebase?
questions.explanation: Discuss: Listening before proposing changes, delivering on commitments reliably, thorough code reviews, and admitting knowledge gaps humbly.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you insisted on 'Highest Standards' and refused to compromise on software quality despite intense release date pressure.
questions.explanation: Show: Advocating for automated testing, load benchmarks, and security audits to avoid production defects.

extra.hr_dimension: Amazon LP: Insist on the Highest Standards

If 60% of writes are standard and 40% are transactional, what is the maximum total write requests per second achievable? [AMAZON Version]
questions.explanation: Average WCU per write = 0.60 * 1 + 0.40 * 2 = 1.4 WCU. Maximum writes/sec = 800 / 1.4 = 571.4 writes/sec.

questions.question: In Amazon S3, standard storage availability SLA is 99.99% per month. In a 30-day month (43,200 minutes), what is the maximum permissible total downtime before an SLA credit is triggered? [AMAZON Version]
questions.explanation: Downtime allowed = 43,200 minutes * (1 - 0.9999) = 43,200 * 0.0001 = 4.32 minutes per month.

questions.question: An Amazon seller increases product price by 25% for holiday surge, then offers a 20% discount coupon. Compared to the original baseline price, what is the net price percentage change? [AMAZON Version]
questions.explanation: Let price = 100. Increased = 125. Discount = 20% of 125 = 25. Final price = 100. Net change = 0%.

questions.question: An Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group has a scale-out policy triggered when average CPU > 75%. Currently 4 instances run at [80%, 70%, 90%, 60%] CPU. What must the 5th instance's CPU be to bring the cluster average down to exactly 65%? [AMAZON Version]
questions.explanation: Current total CPU = 80 + 70 + 90 + 60 = 300%. For 5 instances with average 65%: total needed = 5 * 65 = 325%. 5th instance = 325 - 300 = 25%.

questions.question: A retail warehouse worker can pack 18 small parcels/hr or 12 large parcels/hr. In an 8-hour shift, if the worker packs twice as many small parcels as large parcels, how many total parcels were packed? [AMAZON Version]
questions.explanation: Let x be number of large parcels, 2x small parcels. Time for large = x / 12, time for small = 2x / 18 = x / 9. Total time: x/12 + x/9 = 7x/36 = 8 hours => x ≈ 41 large, 82 small = approx 120-123 parcels.

questions.question: An AWS Kinesis Data Stream has 4 shards. Each shard supports up to 1 MB/s write and 2 MB/s read. If 2 consumer applications independently read the stream in real-time, what is the maximum aggregated write capacity before sharding is required? [AMAZON Version]
questions.explanation: Write capacity is strictly 1 MB/s per shard regardless of consumer count. With 4 shards: 4 * 1 MB/s = 4 MB/s.

questions.question: Amazon SQS standard queue delivers messages at least once. If duplicate probability is 2% per message, what is the probability that in a batch of 10 messages, at least one message is delivered duplicate? [AMAZON Version]

questions.question: An e-commerce flash sale server experiences traffic scaling according to T(t) = 500 + 40t - 2t^2 requests/sec. At what time t (in seconds) does peak request throughput occur? [AMAZON Version]

questions.question: Amazon Aurora database replication clones data across 3 Availability Zones with 6 copies. For a write to succeed, a quorum of 4 out of 6 nodes must acknowledge. If each node has a 98% write success rate, what is the probability that write quorum is achieved? [AMAZON Version]
questions.explanation: Binomial distribution for n=6, p=0.98, k>=4. The likelihood of having 3 or more failures is negligible: C(6,3)*0.02^3 ≈ 0.00016. Success probability is 99.98%.

questions.question: A product recommendation engine computes cosine similarity between user vector U=[3, 4] and product vector V=[4, 3]. What is the exact cosine similarity? [AMAZON Version]
questions.explanation: Dot product = 3*4 + 4*3 = 12 + 12 = 24. Magnitude U = sqrt(9+16)=5. Magnitude V = sqrt(16+9)=5. Cosine similarity = 24 / (5 * 5) = 24 / 25 = 0.96.

questions.question: A team of 6 engineers must be divided into a 2-pizza team of at least 3 but at most 5 engineers. How many different valid sub-teams can be selected? [AMAZON Version]
